cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Declare Allegiance
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you wear my ribbon or Nina's for the chess club election?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Keep us both as friends. Which one do you want as chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I wear yours today and hers tomorrow?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's the vote. Tell me which ribbon you'll wear then; I'll happily lend you the other one today.

mechanism: A treats B friendship and display schedule as permissions A can grant, while insisting the decisive vote-day sign choose one candidate.
confusable: Friendly inclusion is not D58 unless B must commit to a particular side at the consequential moment.
comparison: Visible election ribbons with a friendship compromise differ from proposal ownership in a meeting.
seedUse: Use D58-b timing distinction; avoid assuming A owns Nina ribbon when no line supplies it.
